statusText: EA_ON / green: Nasdaq futures are modestly firmer and crude has eased, while elevated front-end yields and Middle East risk keep Stress extreme; no verified granular NQ sequence shows persistent mean-reversion failure.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains below WATCH; the U.S. cash-open transition is the principal conditional price-path checkpoint.
headline: Modest futures gains and easing oil keep Tail low despite elevated yields and geopolitical Stress
body: Reuters reported Nasdaq futures up 0.6%, S&P 500 futures up 0.4%, the U.S. 2-year yield at 4.7604%, and WTI near $98.15 as Middle East supply flows improved. U.S.-China talks produced incremental proposals but left material issues unresolved. Shared Finviz context is stale and partial. No granular NQ sequence verifies repeated extension or failed retracements.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 UTC clock-hours, Tail was mostly 15-19% / green, rose to WATCH at 22:00-23:00 UTC around the Sunday futures reopening, then returned to 19-18% / green from 00:00 through 02:00 UTC as available evidence remained orderly.
outlookSummary: Tail remains low in the current hour because available evidence does not show persistent one-way NQ structure. The primary conditional WATCH window is 12:00-15:00 UTC around the U.S. cash-open transition, with a smaller conditional WATCH checkpoint at 19:00 UTC for power hour.

forecast.analysis: If the overnight bid stays modest rather than accelerating, Tail should remain low; elevated front-end yields and Gulf headlines keep Stress extreme while price-path confirmation remains limited.
Conditional risk remains centered on whether early European participation reinforces or fades the overnight tech bid; without repeated extension or shallow pullbacks, Tail stays below WATCH.
drivers: Retracement quality remains the Tail test

forecast.analysis: As European liquidity deepens, a two-way tape would support low Tail despite high macro Stress; a clean directional acceleration without retracement would be the main invalidation.
Thin Japanese holiday liquidity still limits inference. Continued orderly trade would keep Tail low, while a sudden gap-extension sequence would matter more than the headline backdrop alone.
drivers: Gap-extension risk matters more than headline count

forecast.analysis: Approaching the European morning, the key conditional test is whether tech strength broadens or stalls. Mixed cross-asset signals favor Stress over Tail unless NQ begins holding persistently near extremes.

If European equity participation remains constructive but not one-way, Tail should stay low. Persistent front-end yield pressure remains a volatility amplifier rather than standalone mean-reversion-failure evidence.
drivers: No automatic Tail increase from yields alone

forecast.analysis: The pre-U.S. handoff can increase sensitivity to yields and geopolitical headlines; absent a sustained NQ extension with weak retracements, the mapped state remains below WATCH.
drivers: Need observed NQ persistence for higher Tail

forecast.analysis: Risk rises into U.S. premarket liquidity. Tail approaches WATCH only if the existing overnight gain is reinforced by directional breadth, semis and failed pullbacks rather than merely higher volatility.
drivers: Semis and breadth confirmation matter conditionally

forecast.analysis: The 12:00 UTC hour enters the cash-open danger window. A widening gap or shallow premarket retracement would raise path risk; balanced price discovery would keep the WATCH state contained.
drivers: Gap persistence is conditional, not assumed

forecast.analysis: The 13:00 UTC hour spans the U.S. cash open. This is the peak conditional Tail window: persistent opening-auction continuation, failed pullbacks and aligned semis/yields would be the decisive escalation evidence.
drivers: Failed pullbacks would be decisive Tail evidence

forecast.analysis: Post-open risk remains WATCH while the first retracement quality becomes observable. Meaningful two-way trade would argue for rapid Tail normalization; repeated extension after failed pullbacks would do the opposite.
drivers: Two-way trade would reduce Tail quickly

forecast.analysis: By 15:00 UTC the base case assumes the opening impulse has had time to retrace. WATCH persists only conditionally if one-way structure remains efficient and NQ continues to hold near session extremes.
drivers: Session-extreme holding would keep Tail elevated

forecast.analysis: If the cash session develops normal retracements and broader two-way trade, Tail should fall below WATCH; Stress can remain high because yields and Middle East risk are still material.
drivers: Yields and Gulf risk keep Stress high

forecast.analysis: Mid-session structure is expected to be less event-sensitive. Tail remains low unless a fresh catalyst produces repeated extension and suppresses meaningful mean reversion.
drivers: Fresh catalyst needed for renewed Tail escalation

forecast.analysis: The afternoon transition can reprice yields or geopolitical headlines, but without renewed one-way NQ structure those factors mainly sustain Stress rather than Tail.
drivers: Tail depends on renewed one-way structure

forecast.analysis: Power-hour approach lifts conditional Tail back to WATCH. A late-session trend extension with shallow pullbacks and reinforcing semis/breadth would be the key failure mode; otherwise the risk window should stay narrow.
After the main power-hour checkpoint, the base case returns below WATCH if the cash session closes with ordinary retracements rather than persistent directional efficiency.
Early post-close conditions should normalize further if no unresolved catalyst is generating a second directional leg; elevated macro uncertainty can keep Stress high without forcing Tail higher.
The late U.S. evening is conditionally calmer. Tail stays low unless a fresh geopolitical or policy discontinuity creates a new one-way futures move.
drivers: No scheduled event implies automatic Tail escalation

forecast.analysis: Into the Asian reopen, normal two-way trade would keep Tail low; any large gap should be judged by subsequent retracement quality rather than gap size alone.
drivers: Judge gap by follow-through and retracements

forecast.analysis: Asian-session risk remains low in the base case, with attention on whether technology leadership persists without becoming a no-retracement trend.
drivers: No-retracement trend would invalidate low-Tail base case

forecast.analysis: If cross-asset conditions stabilize and oil remains off its highs, Tail should remain low even with elevated yields; a fresh aligned catalyst stack would invalidate that assumption.
drivers: Oil stabilization would reduce cross-asset pressure
Elevated yields remain a Stress amplifier

forecast.analysis: The final forecast hour retains a low-Tail base case. Any escalation would require new observed evidence of persistent one-way NQ structure, not the scheduled calendar or generic volatility alone.
drivers: Require new observed one-way NQ evidence for escalation
Calendar importance alone does not raise Tail

forecastDetail.comment: Current evidence shows modestly firmer futures and lower oil, but no verified persistent NQ mean-reversion failure.
Low Tail persists conditionally if the overnight bid remains orderly rather than accelerating into a one-way move.
European participation is the next structure checkpoint; repeated extension, not headline importance, would matter for Tail.
Deeper European liquidity should clarify whether gains remain two-way or become directionally efficient.
Holiday-thinned Asian liquidity limits confidence in path inference; subsequent retracement quality remains decisive.
The European morning should keep Tail low unless tech strength broadens into persistent, weak-retracement NQ continuation.
